MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 24, 2026
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on March 24, 2026, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 19, 2026, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez (arrived 5:03 pm)
  Mayor Bucknum
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  Tarquin Preziosi, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

 At the hour of 5:00 pm Mayor Bucknum recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:00 pm Mayor
 Bucknum reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

 INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

City Council Minutes  1  March 24, 2026
  PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Recognize Mission Viejo 13U Pop Warner Football Team and Cheer Team

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation to League President Julie McRee

 P2.  Recognize the Mission Viejo Rotary Club

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation to President LaVal Brewer and incoming
  President Jay Minor.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tom Moore, M.V.: Asked that the City remain impartial when requests from outside clubs and
associations come before Commissions or the Council with certain requests. Suggested that the
City create a Park Ranger position for the areas of Marguerite Parkway on the East, Alicia Parkway
to the North, Olympia to the East, Oso Parkway to the South and outlined the duties of this position.

Debra Lewandowski, M.V.: Spoke out against the Vista Del Lago Apartment project and asked
that transparency, adherence to housing and zoning laws, public safety assurances and exploration
of alternatives that respect neighborhoods.

Barbara Casserly, M.V.: Thanked the City Council for providing the community with the
immigration resources page on the city’s website and thanked Mayor Bucknum for recognizing
non-profit organizations in our City.

Stephanie Quintino, Laguna Niguel: Thanked the Council for the immigration resource page on
the city’s website and spoke on the devastating deportation of her parents.

Denis Meadow, M.V.: Spoke out against the Vista Del Lago Apartment project and asked for more
transparency with the community.

CONSENT CALENDAR

 Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to approve the
 Consent Calendar outlined below.

 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
 NOES:  None
 ABSENT:  None

  for the City Council's next scheduled regular meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Goodell, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None

  Received written report.

 17. Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) Report

  Received report.

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 City Manager Lister explained that State housing laws heavily limit local control. Cities cannot
 deny or reduce the density of housing projects that comply with zoning and objective standards.
 SB 330 (Housing Crisis Act) strengthens these rules by: Imposing strict timelines for project
 review, Limiting how many times projects can be delayed in meetings, and requiring objective
 (clear, measurable) standards, not subjective judgments. She further explained that the Density
 Bonus Law allows developers to build more units in exchange for affordable housing, including
 major concessions and waivers—even if cities are uncomfortable with them. AB 130 and similar
 laws streamline approvals and can exempt certain projects from environmental review if they
 meet zoning rules. Denying compliant projects is extremely difficult and risky for cities. The
 consequences of noncompliance can lead to loss of certified Housing Element (state approval),
 exposure to the Builder’s Remedy, which allows developers to bypass local zoning, increased
 risk of lawsuits, which cities often lose, and significant financial costs. State oversight is active
 and real, cities that fall out of compliance are closely monitored and pressured to fix issues
 quickly.

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

City Council Minutes  6  March 24, 2026
  City Attorney Preziosi shared that Housing laws (Density Bonus Law & SB 330) make it
 extremely difficult for cities to deny or modify projects. The only possible way to block or reduce
 a project is by proving a serious health or safety risk, but this is a very high legal standard, and
 courts have not supported cities on this basis. He indicated a separate issue that southern
 California Edison has filed a lawsuit seeking refunds on property taxes, claiming wildfire risks
 have reduced the value of its property. The lawsuit involves the California State Board of
 Equalization and multiple counties, including Orange County, Los Angeles County, and San
 Diego County. The potential impact on cities if the state wins, cities are unaffected, if the State
 loses, cities could have to repay portions of property tax revenue already received and clawed
 back to refund Edison. Cities can choose to intervene in the case, but it is not required. It offers
 limited benefit, unless they want to raise additional legal arguments.

 PUBLIC SAFETY UPDATES

 Captain Larson pointed out that some individuals, often called First Amendment auditors, record
 people in public places (including government buildings and public employees) to exercise their
 rights. He indicated that recording in public is generally legal, if it doesn’t interfere with official
 duties or create safety issues, and there is no expectation of privacy in public spaces. While this
 can make people uncomfortable, the recommended response is to stay calm, avoid confrontation,
 and continue normal activities. If recording becomes disruptive or unsafe, it should be reported
 to authorities. He concluded that public recording is usually lawful, and the best approach is to
 remain calm and only involve authorities if there are safety or interference concerns.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

 Council Member Kelley

 Council Member Kelley attended a League of Cities meeting, where Sheriff Barnes shared
 updates. She reminded residents that Proposition 36 was passed by voters in 2024 to increase
 penalties for certain drug and theft crimes which required significant funding for treatment
 programs and court proceedings, yet it included no permanent funding. Flock cameras have
 helped reduce crime, contributing to a 33% drop in auto theft. She stated that Fentanyl overdose
 deaths in Orange County have decreased by 45%. Sheriff Barnes also pointed out that cities are
 not seeing expected tax revenue from marijuana sales, with illegal cartel activity still dominating.
 There were also legislative updates, with more briefings expected to inform the public. Council
 Member Kelley attended the Reuland Charity Tennis & Pickleball event, which raises money for
 local causes, and the Shamrocks and Shenanigans Night Market, which was well-attended.

 Council Member Ruesch

City Council Minutes  7  March 24, 2026
  Council Member Ruesch reported he had a fantastic time at the Tunnel Concert this past
 Wednesday listening to the Pacific Symphony String Quartet. He said although it was hot day, it
 was cool in the tunnel. He noted that this Saturday is the Marine Lake Day at Lake Mission Viejo
 from 11-4 pm. He encouraged residents to stop by and say hello to our Marines.

 Council Member Vasquez

 Council Member Vasquez stated she was in San Diego for a few days and that her youngest
 daughter turned 10 and had her first slumber party this past weekend.

 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that his son Scott and wife Carissa had a baby girl on
 Sunday. He proudly said this is his eighth grandchild and seventh girl.

 Mayor Bucknum

 Mayor Bucknum attended the Shamrocks and Shenanigans Night Market and the charity flag
 football RX3 Foundation event at Saddleback College supporting multiple charities, especially
 the Jesse Rees Foundation’s “Never Ever Give Up” (NEGU) program, which provides “Joy Jars”
 to children with cancer. She praised the event, including participation from the USA Women’s
 Flag Football team, and encouraged more community attendance next year. She also attended a
 legislative conference in Sacramento with the Southern California Association of Governments,
 where they met with officials including Attorney General Rob Bonta. The discussions focused
 on housing, transportation, environmental policies, funding for regional planning, modernization
 of SB375, and streamlining CEQA to address housing costs and improve transparency. Lastly,
 she shared upcoming community events, including the July 11 “America 250” parade, and
 encouraged participation in local celebrations like the Springtime in Paris event at the Community
 Center this weekend. She closed by wishing everyone a happy Passover, Easter, and spring
 season.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 8:10 pm, with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
 Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Hall of Fame high school football coach and the City’s
 2017 Hometown Hero Bob Johnson to Tuesday, April 14, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.
